title: Ops Reliability Synapse Roadmap - cross-team SLO pilot
body:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for a cross-functional program ("Ops Reliability Synapse") to pilot, validate, and scale SLO practice across three canonical product surfaces: hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments. The goal is to create an operationally lightweight, measurable SLO framework that product teams can adopt with minimum friction and clear rollback/mitigation patterns.

Context / why now:
- We have recurring customer frustration during regional capacity pressure and model-serving latency spikes; no single cross-org playbook exists.
- Platform instrumentation improvements (trace sampling, token-level latency) shipped Q4 2025 — we can now reliably measure per-route latency and error signals.
- Executive priority to reduce sev frequency for inference endpoints by 30% over 12 months.

Program goals (SMART):
- Define 3 canonical SLOs (availability, 95th latency for request path, token-accuracy/quality signal) and roll them into 2 pilot services within 60 days.
- Achieve 90% adoption of SLO dashboards and runbooks in pilot squads within 90 days after pilot start.
- Reduce repeat incident recurrence for pilot services by 25% within 6 months.

Scope (what's in / out):
- In: SLO definition templates, runbooks, monitoring dashboards, canary gating for releases, automated escalation hooks, cost-tagging for SLO alerting.
- Out: full org-wide enforcement, customer-facing SLA changes, deep model evaluation changes (those remain with applied-ml).

High-level approach / phases:
1) Discover & baseline (2 weeks): inventory candidate routes, collect historical metrics, run lightweight blame analysis for incidents.
2) Define & align (2 weeks): converge on SLO definitions per surface, finalize measurement rules and alert thresholds with product leads.
3) Pilot implementation (6 weeks): add SLO metrics to dashboards, create runbooks, integrate automated paging and Slack flow, configure canary gating on deploy pipeline for the pilot services.
4) Observe & iterate (8 weeks): run incident drills, capture signal quality, tune thresholds, and document operational playbooks.
5) Scale plan (quarterly): publish adoption kit, templates, and partner with solutions engineering for outward rollouts.

Canonical SLO candidates (examples):
- Availability: successful responses (HTTP 2xx or domain-specific success) >= 99.5% over 7d window.
- Latency SLO: p95 request-to-first-byte <= 150ms for inference-light routes; p95 <= 400ms for long-context model routes.
- Quality guardrail: regression rate detected by evaluation harness (prompt-set mismatch) < 2% relative to baseline monthly.
(These are starting points. Final thresholds must be approved by product owners.)

Stakeholders & RACI (draft):
- Platform (owner): platform-engineering (Aisha Patel) — SLO templates, automated dashboards, alert plumbing.
- Product owners (R): hosted-api-product, dedicated-product, private-deployments-product — approve SLOs.
- Observability (C): observability team (Sofia Chen) — instrumentation and dashboarding.
- SRE / Oncall (R/C): SRE leads (Liam O'Connor) — runbook validations, drill design.
- Solutions / CS (C): customer-success — customer impact mapping.

Pilot services (initial):
- Hosted API: route group = generation-short-context (high QPS). Owner: hosted-api-product.
- Dedicated: routing/gateway for reserved pools (burst handling). Owner: dedicated-product.
- Private: VPC control-plane health / deployment acceptance (instrumentation light). Owner: private-deployments-product.
(We will begin with Hosted API + Dedicated; Private is optional in phase 1 depending on instrumentation readiness.)

Milestones & rough dates (working):
- Week 0 (kickoff): cross-team kickoff + shared measurement doc (owner: Aisha) — target 2026-02-16.
- Weeks 1-2: baseline collection and incident history digest (owner: Marco).
- Weeks 3-4: SLO definitions & approval workshop (owners: product leads).
- Weeks 5-10: pilot instrument + runbooks + canary gating (owners: platform + observability).
- Weeks 11-18: incident drills, threshold tuning, adoption check (owners: SRE + product).
- Week 19: pilot retro & scale recommendation (owner: Aisha).

Observability / instrumentation checklist (practical TODOs):
- Ensure token-level latency and request metadata are emitted with consistent schema.
- Add per-route tags to traces and metrics (team, product, model, quantization profile).
- Build p95/p50/p99 latency panels and availability panels in a shared dashboard.
- Implement SLO burn-rate calculation and expose a weekly burn report workspace.
- Wire alerting to a dedicated Ops SLO channel with runbook link and automated incident creation.

Runbook outline (template):
- Symptoms: how the issue surfaces (alerts, customer reports, degradation patterns).
- Immediate checks (first 5): routing health, recent deploys, GPU saturation, KV-cache miss rate, model variant fallback events.
- Escalation matrix: oncall -> SRE -> platform eng -> product lead.
- Mitigations: automatic throttling, fallback to cheaper model variant, traffic-shift to regional pool, emergency rollback.
- Postmortem triggers: SLO breach > 4h or repeated breach within 30d.

Gating & enforcement (practical policy):
- Canary gating: any deploy that would increase error budget burn by >20% in a rolling 1h window must fail canary and page.
- Release checklist: SLO metrics present for the route, runbook attached, oncall aware.
- Soft enforcement in pilot: platform flags but product teams can override with documented rationale during pilot.

Training & adoption:
- 90-min workshop for pilot teams covering: SLO principles, dashboard walkthrough, runbook exercises, drill simulation.
- Short cheat-sheet and Slack bot to link runbooks when SLO alerts trigger.

Risks & mitigations (brief):
- Risk: noisy signals due to sampling gaps -> Mitigation: ramp up full sampling for 72h during baseline, then tune.
- Risk: product teams see SLO as extra ops work -> Mitigation: highlight reduced incident firefighting time, provide platform-managed templates.
- Risk: cost of increased telemetry -> Mitigation: targeted sampling windows + cost tags; measure ROI by incident-hours saved.

Success measurement (end of pilot):
- Technical: dashboards in place, automated alerts wired, runbooks validated by two drills.
- Adoption: pilot squads have playbooks attached to team repos and confirm runbook familiarity in survey (target 90% familiarity).
- Outcome: measurable reduction in incident recurrence and MTTR compared to baseline.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Aisha: finalize kickoff invite + measurement doc (due 2026-02-16).
- Marco: export 90d incident history for hosted-api + dedicated (due 2026-02-18).
- Sofia: draft dashboard skeleton and list of missing telemetry events (due 2026-02-20).
- Product leads: confirm pilot route owners and approve time commitment for drills.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Decide whether quality guardrail SLO is measured via offline evals or live feedback signal; need input from applied-ml.
- If burn-rate gating ties into CI, confirm with release-eng for safe failure mode.
- Consider a lightweight billing metric to tag SLO alert cost impact (for exec reporting).

Meeting log (scratch):
- 2026-02-12 sync: scoped initial pilot to hosted + dedicated; private will follow if VPC control-plane metrics available.
- 2026-02-13 infra note: trace tag schema needs small change to include "model_variant".

Draft checklist (for pilot readiness):
- [ ] SLO definitions approved by product.
- [ ] Dashboards live in shared folder.
- [ ] Runbooks created and linked in alert.
- [ ] Canary gating enabled for pilot routes.
- [ ] Drill schedule published and participants confirmed.

Notes on tone: keep this doc as a working plan; expect many edits. Use this as the single source of truth for pilot decisions until formal playbook is published.

-- end of draft --
